content.title: About
content.content: Pepperoni pizza is a popular school lunch option. A medium crust provides a crunchy base, while slices of spicy pepperoni add flavor and a hint of heat. The pizza is served hot, often with tomato sauce and a modest amount of cheese.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pepperoni is an American version of Italian salami, made from pork and beef.
A medium crust is considered ideal for balancing crispness and softness.
Pizza is frequently included in school menus as a quick source of carbs and protein.
Tomato sauce in pizza is rich in lycopene, an antioxidant that retains its bright red color when baked.
Some schools bake pizza in specialized ovens that reach the required temperature quickly.

items.title: Protein source
items.content: Pepperoni and cheese provide a substantial amount of protein needed for growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Energy supply
items.content: Carbohydrates from the crust give a rapid source of energy, important for active students.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The dough and meat ingredients contain vitamins B1, B2 and B6, supporting metabolism.

items.title: Lycopene in tomato sauce
items.content: Lycopene has antioxidant properties and may help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Calcium from cheese
items.content: Cheese adds calcium, essential for bone and tooth development in children.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Salt in the sauce and pepperoni can lead to exceeding the daily recommended sodium intake.

items.title: Saturated fats
items.content: Meat toppings and cheese contain saturated fats, which should be consumed in moderation.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Cheese may trigger allergic reactions in children with lactose intolerance or milk protein allergy.

items.title: Monosodium glutamate
items.content: Some sauces may contain added MSG, which can cause headaches in sensitive individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Pepperoni pizza is typically eaten hot, cut into serving slices. Adding fresh vegetables such as tomatoes or arugula can balance flavor and boost nutrient content.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftover pizza in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. Reheat in an oven or microwave to restore crust crispness.
